executive_summary: USD/CHF trades at 0.8066 (close of 2026-08-06), meaning one US dollar buys 0.8066 Swiss francs; a rising pair is dollar strength and franc weakness. The pair is up 0.15% over one month, 2.53% over three, 1.00% over six and 0.77% over twelve — a flat year that conceals a violent round trip through a 0.76069 low in late January and a 0.82072 high on 29 July, leaving spot at the 71st percentile of its 52-week range. The dominant bilateral narrative is the single widest policy differential in the developed world: a Federal Reserve at a 3.50–3.75% target range with three sitting hike dissenters against a Swiss National Bank pinned at 0.00% and publishing a conditional inflation forecast built on zero through 2028, for a static +362.5bp gap and a +427.5bp ten-year spread. That configuration has reassigned the franc from haven to the world's cheapest funding currency, with ING noting that Switzerland's low-rate environment has made USD/CHF a very popular vehicle for expressing hawkish Fed views. What diverges most from the two standalone dossiers is that the USD dossier's own weakest link — a 5.27% thirty-year Treasury and a 5.8%-of-GDP deficit — collides head-on with the franc's greatest strength, a 9.77%-of-GDP current-account surplus and a 37.6% debt-to-GDP AAA sovereign, producing a fiscal-quality differential that is far more binding bilaterally than it is against any other G10 counterpart. We are Bullish USD/CHF tactically at conviction 4 (weighted score +0.4020, confidence 60%) and Bullish strategically at conviction 2 (+0.1336, confidence 58%), with the thesis decaying rather than compounding across horizons. The caveat is explicit and important: this is a carry-and-funding trade, not a fundamental one — on spot alone the six-month risk/reward is 0.27:1, and the pair's adverse distribution is fat-tailed because both legs are havens and the franc is the more sensitive of the two.

market_context.valuation_assessment: On the BIS real effective measure, the two currencies are unusually close to fair value simultaneously, which removes valuation as a constraint in either direction. The Swiss REER at 101.69 for June 2026 sits at the 40th percentile of its own recent window and 0.1% below its window mean, having fallen 2.5% from a 104.3 February peak. The US broad REER at 107.84 sits within roughly one percent of its own five-year average on either of two competing derivations, with the sign of the residual unresolved. The bilateral read-across from the dossiers' own REER-differential tables is a modest franc undervaluation against the dollar: the USD dossier computes the dollar 0.91% cheap versus CHF (implied USD/CHF fair value 0.8151), while the CHF dossier computes the franc 5.7% cheap versus USD (implied 0.7642). Those two estimates bracket spot in opposite directions and cannot both be right; the honest bilateral conclusion is that USD/CHF is within a few percent of real fair value at 0.8066 and that mean reversion supplies no tradeable edge at either horizon.

market_context.recent_regime: The regime since May has been a carry-on, haven-off environment in which USD/CHF has functioned as the market's chosen expression of a hawkish Fed. The transmission is mechanical: a zero-rate SNB, a Fed with three sitting hike dissenters, VIX at 17.09, US high-yield spreads at 284bp, the S&P 500 at 7,489.72 and gold down 17.94% over six months together describe conditions in which the franc's haven function is dormant and its funding function dominant. The two-day reversal on 29-30 July is the regime's first real stress test, and it came not from a franc-positive shock but from the dollar leg — the DXY lost the 100 handle on 30 July with a -1.01% session on fiscal term-premium concerns. This pair now falls for US reasons rather than Swiss ones.

bilateral_carry_analysis.breakeven_move: 362.5bp of annualised carry is approximately 27 pips per month; a long-USD/short-CHF position breaks even against the forward if spot falls to 0.80393 within one month, 0.79849 within three months and 0.78994 within six months — franc appreciations of 0.33%, 1.00% and 2.07% respectively.
bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The USD/CHF carry differential is +362.5 basis points annualised, the widest policy-rate gap between any two G10 currencies and the deepest carry cushion available anywhere in the developed FX complex. It is composed of a Federal Reserve target range of 3.50–3.75% against an SNB policy rate of 0.00%, and it is static rather than drifting, with the SNB's own June 2026 conditional inflation forecast constructed on a 0% policy-rate assumption across the entire three-year horizon. The term-structure differential is wider still at +427.5bp on the 10Y and +414bp at 2Y. Carry-to-vol at 0.54 is more than double EUR/USD's 0.26 and comfortably the best risk-adjusted carry in the G10 dollar complex, making USD/CHF the point on the efficient frontier where absolute carry and vol-adjusted carry are simultaneously near-optimal. The carry regime is working, evidenced by VIX at 17.09, HY OAS at 284bp, and equities near records, but the regime's fragility is clear: exceptionally low FX volatility is unlikely to last, and a larger energy or equity shock could quickly revive demand for the franc. The forward-implied franc appreciation of roughly 4% annualised exceeds the 362.5bp policy spread by 34-49bp, a disclosed gap attributable to SARON fixing below zero, US money-market rates above the funds midpoint, and an unobservable cross-currency basis — a disclosed gap, not a free lunch.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: At +362.5bp the USD/CHF policy differential is the widest bilateral gap in the G10, and the framework's high-carry rule (200bp) explicitly contemplates a +0.03 to +0.05 boost. For this pair the rate differential is not one input among ten — it is the transmission mechanism through which almost every other factor expresses itself.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The differential is +362.5bp on policy rates, +414bp at the two-year point and +427.5bp at the ten-year, and every one of those gaps is wider than it was a month ago because US yields rose while Swiss yields were anchored by a central bank that has publicly assumed zero for three years. The trajectory over the tactical window is one-directional: the SNB does not meet until 24 September, so there is no scheduled mechanism by which the Swiss leg can change inside the horizon, while the Fed's 29 July hold drew three dissents in favour of a 25bp increase and the June SEP median of 3.8% for end-2026 implies one hike is the Committee's own central case. The pricing question is where the mispricing sits, and it is on the Swiss side: the most recent obtainable OIS snapshot embeds roughly +12bp of SNB tightening by December and +24bp by March 2027 against an institution whose own conditional forecast conditions on a flat zero through 2028, and each basis point of that premium that decays is a marginal pair-positive with no offsetting mechanism. The transmission to this pair is unusually direct because there is no intervening variable — USD/CHF is quite literally the price of the Fed-SNB spread, with no commodity, equity or trade channel of comparable strength. The counterweight, and the reason confidence is 70 rather than 80, is empirical: the pair has appreciated only 0.77% over twelve months while paying 362.5bp of carry, which means spot has moved roughly 285bp AGAINST the differential over the year. A differential this wide that has failed to transmit for four quarters is not a mechanical certainty.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the gap is scheduled to widen rather than merely persist, which is a genuinely rare configuration for a differential already at 362.5bp. On the Swiss side there is no plausible path to compression: all but one of 29 forecasters expect the SNB to keep rates unchanged through 2026, even as futures markets price in a hike by December, and Pictet's lead economist has argued the bar for negative rates remains higher than in 2015. On the US side the June SEP median implies +17.5bp by end-2026, so the base case takes the differential to roughly 387.5bp by December. The trajectory then turns ambiguous beyond the horizon, since the Fed's own dots embed -20bp in 2027 and -20bp in 2028, but that compression sits outside the six-month window. The pricing question strategically is different from tactically: the forward curve at six months implies 0.78994, i.e. it pays a holder of dollars 2.07% over the period simply for the differential. The strategic risk to this factor is the US long end: a 5.27% thirty-year with 2.28% breakevens means the market is charging a rising term premium on the reserve asset, and July demonstrated that a currency can weaken while its carry advantage widens if the yield rise is fiscal in character.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: For this specific pair the inflation and growth differential is enormous but almost entirely inert, because the SNB has pre-committed to not responding to Swiss data and the Fed has pre-committed to not responding dovishly to US data. A differential that cannot change either reaction function within the horizon deserves less weight than the framework default assumes.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential is the widest in the developed world and it is about to widen further on base effects. US headline CPI is 3.5% and core PCE 3.3% against Swiss headline CPI of 0.5% and SFSO core inflation 1 of just 0.3% — a 300bp headline gap and a 300bp core gap. The trajectory inside the window is asymmetric in the pair's favour: June US headline CPI fell 0.4% month-on-month entirely because energy dropped 5.7% during the brief post-ceasefire oil collapse, and with Brent having traded from $86.99 to $105.32 and back to $91.82 through July, the 12 August print mechanically re-accelerates toward 3.7–4.0%. The Swiss July print faces the mirror-image base effect, so the two economies are set to report inflation moving in opposite directions in the same fortnight. On growth the differential is +151bp and Switzerland's leg is deteriorating for a dated, bilateral reason: Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs at a 15% capped rate took effect for Swiss Annex III companies on 31 July, striking the largest single Swiss export line to the United States. The transmission to the pair runs through real rates: the US real policy rate is +12.5bp against a Swiss real policy rate of -50bp, a +62.5bp real differential that widens if US headline re-accelerates while Swiss headline fades. The offsetting tactical risk is that US Q2 GDP came in at 1.5% annualised against 2.1% in Q1 and June payrolls added only 57,000 with 74,000 of downward revisions, so a soft 7 August print would hit the base leg hard with no positioning cushion beneath it.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the growth and inflation differentials both compress, and they compress from opposite ends in a way that produces a genuine standoff rather than a weak directional call. On the US side, the energy base effect washes out within one to two quarters, the Dallas Fed trimmed mean is only 2.2% and core CPI has decelerated to 2.6%, so the 3.3% core PCE overshoot is narrow rather than broad. On the Swiss side the direction is the reverse: the SNB revised its conditional forecast UP to 0.6/0.6/0.7 from 0.5/0.5/0.6, Brent at $91.82 is 25% above its year-ago level, and the SNB explicitly warned that stronger second-round effects are possible. A US disinflation converging toward 2.2% while Swiss inflation drifts toward 0.7-0.9% compresses the headline gap from 300bp toward roughly 150bp, which is straightforwardly pair-negative. Growth runs the other way: US Q2 at 1.5% annualised is converging DOWN toward Swiss trend while the pharma tariff extension on 29 September and the USD 200bn Swiss corporate investment pledge both cut Swiss growth further. An inflation convergence that is pair-negative running alongside a growth divergence that is pair-positive, at a factor weight of only 0.08, is exactly a zero.

Over one to six months that base effect exhausts itself and Swiss inflation drifts up on imported energy, so the differential compresses in a way that offsets the widening growth gap.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: USD/CHF is a haven-versus-haven pair, which makes its risk beta structurally muted relative to something like AUD/JPY but does not make it zero — the franc is the more risk-sensitive of the two havens, so the pair falls in genuine risk-off and rises in risk-on. The current regime is unambiguously risk-on: the S&P 500 closed at 7,489.72, US investment-grade spreads are 80bp and high yield 284bp, and VIX is 17.09 having spiked to 20.66 on FOMC day before retracing within a single session. The single most informative cross-asset input for this specific pair is gold, because CHF and gold share a debasement-and-uncertainty demand function while the dollar sits on the other side of the trade: XAU/USD at $4,054 is down 12.14% over three months and 17.94% over six from a February peak, which is direct evidence that the haven complex to which the franc belongs is being liquidated. The complication that separates this pair from the standalone dossiers is that both currencies benefit from risk aversion, so the relevant question is which haven wins — the franc on genuine capital-flight events, the dollar on liquidity-scramble events. The current tail is a Middle East escalation, a capital-flight event and therefore franc-positive on the risk channel, though the dollar recaptures some of that through the terms-of-trade channel because the United States is a net energy exporter. Net tactical read: the regime is pair-positive, the tail is pair-negative, and the tail is not currently active.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the risk channel is genuinely two-sided for this pair in a way that it is not for a pure risk proxy, and forcing a direction would add noise. The bull branch requires the current configuration to persist for another four to six months, which is not the base case given high-yield at 284bp against a 3.63% funds rate and a Fed priced to hike further. The bear branch — a genuine risk event — resolves pair-negative because the franc's haven response is a capital-flight response that arrives more slowly than the yen's but holds its gains longer, and USD/CHF is unusual among the majors in that the franc carries explicit safe-haven status, so the rate differential sets the running carry but spot can be overwhelmed by safe-haven flows during stress. What partly offsets it is that the dollar has an energy-exporter kicker the franc lacks: a Hormuz re-escalation delivers the US both a haven bid and a terms-of-trade gain while delivering Switzerland a haven bid and a terms-of-trade loss. That netting is why the pair's downside in a geopolitical shock is shallower than the franc's standalone haven beta implies, and why this factor is Neutral rather than Bearish.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The two legs reinforce, which is the amplifying rather than the muting configuration and therefore a genuine tactical negative. Speculators are net long the base currency — ICE USD Index non-commercials +17,197, up 1,583 into the 28 July high — and simultaneously net short the quote currency at -8,897 leveraged and -37,558 asset-manager CHF contracts. Implied USD/CHF length is therefore more crowded than either leg reads alone, and the crowding is concentrated in the dollar leg, which was added to three sessions before the DXY fell 1.5% over 29-31 July. The critical bilateral asymmetry is that the franc leg supplies no squeeze fuel: leveraged funds sit at only the 28th percentile of their range and asset managers at the 76th — near their LEAST short reading — and the legacy non-commercial franc short narrowed from -41.1k in early July to -33.5k by 31 July, five consecutive weeks of covering. That cuts two ways bilaterally: it removes the classic short-squeeze cap on the pair, but it also means the pair's recent advance was carried by a crowded dollar long that has no fresh buyer beneath it. A soft 7 August payroll print hits the base leg with no cushion, and that is the tactical negative.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a one-to-six-month horizon the futures data stops mattering and the structural cross-border flow takes over, and for this pair that flow is unusually well identified and unusually one-directional. ING wrote that carry-trade investors will increasingly fund out of Swiss francs rather than the yen, because franc funding is cheaper and avoids the risk of Bank of Japan intervention to the tune of $70bn. That reassignment does not appear in CME data — it appears in cross-border bank lending and the FX swap market — which means the true short-franc, long-dollar position is materially larger than the USD 7.19bn visible on the exchange. On the dollar side the structural flow points the same way: IMF COFER shows the dollar's reserve share rising to 57.13% in 2026Q1 from 56.42%, and TIC recorded $262.8bn of net foreign purchases of long-term US securities in May alone against a $226.8bn quarterly current-account deficit. Two independent structural flows — franc-funded leverage and dollar reserve accumulation — both push this specific pair higher. The offsetting consideration is real: a large share of the street holds the same position through the same low-vol instruments, which means the exit is far narrower than the position size implies.

Tactically the marginal price-setter is the speculative futures community, long the base into a high already marked against — a negative. Strategically the price is set by cross-border funding books and reserve managers, both structurally buying dollars against francs. The transition point is roughly the four-to-eight-week period around the 16 September FOMC.

As a signal, current positioning is mildly bearish for the pair tactically, because the dollar long has no fresh buyer beneath it while the franc short has already been substantially covered without any corresponding franc appreciation.

strategic.combined_positioning_signal: At a strategic horizon the contrarian question is what the other side sees, and for this pair the franc bull's case is coherent: a 9.77%-of-GDP current-account surplus, a CHF 974bn net international investment position, an AAA sovereign at 37.6% debt-to-GDP and a real effective exchange rate at only the 40th percentile.

strategic.contrarian_case: That coherent franc-bull case is why the strategic weighted score is +0.134 rather than +0.40. The counterweight specific to this pair is that there is no crowded strategic dollar SHORT to squeeze either — COFER is rising and TIC inflows are large — so the pair lacks the two-sided squeeze dynamics of, say, USD/JPY. tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external balance differential is one of the largest in the G10 and it runs decisively against the pair — the United States runs a current-account deficit of 2.9% of GDP while Switzerland runs a surplus of 9.77%, a 12.67-percentage-point gap — but that stock differential has no tactical transmission mechanism. What does transmit inside four weeks is the commodity channel, and there the netting is unambiguous. Oil up is a mild-to-moderate positive for the dollar because the United States is now a net energy exporter earning a $63.61 Gulf Coast 3-2-1 crack spread, and a clear negative for the franc because Switzerland has zero domestic hydrocarbon production; net effect of Brent at $91.82, up 30.3% from $70.46 at end-June, is a rising pair. Gold runs the same way: gold down 17.94% over six months is a negative for the franc through the shared haven-and-debasement demand function; net effect is again a rising pair. There is no third commodity of consequence for this pair, which makes the netting unusually clean. The bilateral trade relationship is structurally franc-positive but does not move on a four-week timescale. On balance the two active commodity channels both push the pair higher while the dormant stock differential pushes it lower, and over two to four weeks the active channels win.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.16 weight this is the largest single counterweight to the carry thesis and it is the reason the strategic score is a third of the tactical one. The stock differential is severe and structural: the United States carries a net international investment position of -$21.27tn against Switzerland's +CHF 974bn net creditor position, and runs a 2.9%-of-GDP external deficit against a 9.77% surplus. The bilateral trade relationship reinforces it: IMF DOTS shows US goods exports to Switzerland of $25.0bn against imports from Switzerland of $63.7bn in 2024, for a net US goods deficit of $38.6bn. Against that stand three dated, quantified pair-positive offsets: the energy terms-of-trade transfer persists with Gulf production ~11.4mb/d below pre-war and full flows not resuming until 2027; the 15% Section 232 pharma tariff extends to all importers on 29 September; and the USD 200bn Swiss corporate US investment pledge is by construction a franc-selling, dollar-buying capital outflow. Netting these against a 12.67-percentage-point current-account gap, the offsets compress the Swiss surplus by perhaps 1-2 percentage points of GDP over several years, taking it from roughly 10% to roughly 8% — a reduction, not a reversal.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the widest guidance divergence available anywhere in the G10 and it is the cleanest bilateral signal in the dossier. On the base side, the 29 July FOMC statement ends with the flat declarative that the Committee will deliver price stability, the June minutes record that most participants preferred to remove the easing bias entirely, and the vote moved from a unanimous 12-0 hold on 17 June to a 9-3 hold on 29 July with all three dissenters wanting a 25bp increase. On the quote side, the SNB has done the exact opposite of guiding: it published a three-year conditional inflation forecast constructed on a 0% policy-rate assumption and declared that forecast satisfactory, a pre-commitment to inaction. Chairman Schlegel stated the SNB has an increased willingness to intervene in the foreign exchange market if necessary — one-directional guidance aimed only at franc strength, with no symmetric language about franc weakness. The bilateral consequence is that the pair's base currency has policy optionality skewed hawkish while its quote currency has none at all. Credibility runs the same way: all but one of 29 forecasters expect the SNB to hold through 2026 even as futures price a hike by December, so the sell side believes the SNB more than the market does. The sequencing matters tactically: no SNB communication event falls inside the window, while the Fed produces payrolls, CPI, minutes and Jackson Hole — four opportunities for the base leg to reinforce and zero for the quote leg to respond.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months guidance carries a 0.12 weight and becomes the binding constraint on the pair's floor rather than mere context. The SNB has removed itself as a source of positive surprise for the franc, and did so publicly and datably: source stories that the SNB will keep its policy rate unchanged at 0.00% until the end of 2027 hit the Swiss franc in late July, the event that converted the franc from a cyclical low-yielder into a structural funding currency. The Fed's guidance runs the other way and is institutionally entrenched — five external task forces, a reaffirmed Statement on Longer-Run Goals, and a Chair who has staked his tenure on 2%. The strategic complication is intervention: UBS judges that foreign exchange interventions are possible but will remain selective, and that the conditions for a sustained weakening of the franc are not in place — an SNB that intervenes only against franc strength caps the pair's downside but supplies no upside, so the guidance asymmetry is a floor-setter rather than a driver. The constraint on that behaviour has also loosened bilaterally: the US Treasury retained Switzerland on its currency monitoring list but Switzerland now meets only one of three criteria, so a less constrained SNB is a marginal pair-positive. The genuine two-way risk is the SNB's own history: a three-person Governing Board meeting four times a year with minimal forward guidance retains real capacity to surprise, and January 2015 remains the reference for how discontinuous that surprise can be.

The market simultaneously holds hawkish franc premium as a hedge and runs the largest franc-funded long-dollar position of the cycle — logically inconsistent positions that resolve in our favour as the premium decays.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: The dominant live geopolitical binary — Hormuz — affects both legs of this pair in the same direction through the haven channel and in opposite directions through the terms-of-trade channel, so its net bilateral impact is materially smaller than its impact on either currency standalone. There is also no bilateral political risk between the United States and Switzerland beyond the already-settled tariff file.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The event calendar is genuinely two-sided for this pair in a way it is not for either dossier alone, because the same events hit both legs. The dominant binary is the Strait of Hormuz, where the 60-day no-charge transit window under Article 5 of the 17 June US-Iran memorandum expires around 16 August. Escalation delivers the dollar a haven bid plus a terms-of-trade gain and delivers the franc a haven bid plus a terms-of-trade loss — the haven components substantially cancel, leaving the terms-of-trade differential as the net, mildly pair-positive at Brent below roughly $110 and turning pair-negative above it. The genuinely bilateral event on the calendar has already landed and is franc-negative: the 15% capped Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff took effect for Annex III Swiss companies on 31 July. Against that, the base leg carries dated negatives the quote leg does not — the 3 and 5 August Treasury refunding events, which transmit via the fiscal term-premium channel that produced the 29-30 July reversal. Swiss domestic political risk is close to nil inside the window. Netting a landed franc-negative against live dollar-negative supply events and a two-sided geopolitical binary produces no directional edge at a 0.03 weight.

The pair-positive calendar is Swiss: the full pharmaceutical tariff extension to all importers on 29 September, and the cumulative drag of the USD 200bn investment pledge. The pair-negative calendar is American and unusually dense: federal appropriations expire on 30 September against a base rate that already includes a partial DHS shutdown; the midterms fall on 3 November; three US-China suspensions expire simultaneously on 10 November; and two undecided appeals sit over the tariff architecture including roughly $166bn of IEEPA refunds. Historically US political stress transmits to USD/CHF through the haven channel more directly than to almost any other dollar pair, because the franc is the primary alternative store of value when US institutional quality is questioned — the single most important bilateral asymmetry in this factor. The Hormuz tail persists across the whole window. A pair-positive Swiss trade calendar of known and capped magnitude against a pair-negative US political calendar of unknown magnitude, with an undated geopolitical binary whose sign depends on scale, is a genuine Neutral.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Fiscal risk is normally background for both legs of a G10 pair; here it is tactically live on one side and structurally inert on the other, producing an unusually clean bilateral signal. The United States closed 31 July with the 30-year at 5.27% and the 20-year at 5.28%, both the highest of 2026, having risen 6bp and 7bp in a single session while ten-year breakevens were flat at 2.28% — a pure term-premium move, the classic signature of fiscal rather than monetary repricing. Switzerland is the mirror image: AAA across agencies, general government debt at 37.6% of GDP, a constitutional debt brake in force since 2003, a 10Y yielding 0.475% and sovereign CDS effectively unquoted. The bilateral spread of 479.5bp between a 5.27% US thirty-year and a 0.475% Swiss ten-year is the widest quality gap this pair can construct, and its direction of travel is one-way. The transmission was demonstrated in the tactical window itself: the pair fell 1.05% on 30 July, the largest single-session decline since April, on a day when US long-end yields rose and the DXY lost the 100 handle — a textbook fiscal-repricing session in which a wider US yield advantage produced a weaker dollar. The proximate catalysts are dated inside the window: Treasury publishes marketable borrowing estimates on 3 August and the quarterly refunding statement on 5 August, against a $997.9bn TGA and a FY2026 YTD deficit of $1.3665tn.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.09 strategic weight this is the highest-confidence negative in the analysis, because the trajectory is knowable on both sides and it is one-way. The CBO's February 2026 baseline puts the US deficit at 5.8% of GDP against a fifty-year average of 3.8%, debt held by the public rising from 101% to 120% of GDP by 2036, and net interest at $1.039tn or 3.3% of GDP rising to 4.6% — and that baseline is already stale in the wrong direction because it predates the Supreme Court's 20 February IEEPA ruling that removed roughly $1.7tn of projected tariff revenue, of which replacements recover less than 60%. Switzerland's trajectory is flat by constitutional design. The bilateral consequence is that the quality gap widens mechanically over the horizon without anyone doing anything, and net interest at 3.3% of GDP is being refinanced at a 5.27% thirty-year rate rather than at the sub-2% coupons rolling off. The specific mechanism by which this hurts the pair is that the franc is the primary alternative reserve-quality asset when US sovereign quality is questioned — more so than the yen or the euro. That makes USD/CHF the single most fiscally exposed dollar cross in the G10. The counterweight is that Swiss sovereign quality is already fully capitalised in a 0.475% ten-year yield — the bond market has paid for the AAA in full, and it is only the FX market that is currently indifferent to it. That indifference is what we expect to erode.

What is unpriced is the CBO baseline revision that must follow the IEEPA ruling, and that when it comes the franc is the specific destination for the resulting reallocation.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This pair sits at the centre of the global funding stack, with the dollar as the asset leg and the franc as the liability leg, which makes Factor 10 unusually direct here. Domestic dollar liquidity has become genuinely scarce: reserve balances fell to $2,944,541mn in the week to 29 July, down $355.2bn on the year, the overnight reverse repo facility is effectively drained at roughly $2bn, the Treasury General Account is at $997.9bn, and SOFR printed 3.65% exactly at IORB with a 75th percentile of 3.70% on $3,011bn of volume. ING wrote that the story points carry investors to increasingly fund out of Swiss francs rather than the yen, because franc funding is cheaper and avoids Bank of Japan intervention risk. Critically this is a plumbing story rather than a credit story — investment-grade spreads are 80bp and high yield 284bp with equities at records — so there is no corroborating stress that would trigger a franc haven bid alongside the funding tightness. Confidence is held to 58 rather than higher by a hard data gap: the three-month USD/CHF cross-currency basis is not obtainable from any free venue this cycle.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the funding factor is genuinely balanced for this pair because the two offsetting policies have already been announced. Quantitative tightening is over — the 29 July directive instructs the Desk to purchase Treasury bills to maintain ample reserves and reinvest all principal, so the effective runoff pace is zero and the balance sheet has grown from $6,724,564mn a month ago to $6,738,190mn. On the Treasury side the General Account normalises from a late-July peak of roughly $1tn toward the guided $950bn end-September balance, adding reserves back, while a $671bn July-September borrowing requirement drains them through bill issuance. Those three forces net to approximately zero over the horizon, which is the definition of a Neutral. The bilateral overlay is what makes this different from a generic USD assessment: the franc's role as the marginal funding currency is a function of relative rates and relative intervention risk, both stable over the horizon, so the liability leg of the trade stays cheap regardless of what US reserves do. The specific strategic risk is seasonal and dated: cross-currency basis conventionally widens into the December year-end turn as bank balance sheets are constrained, and a franc-funded long-dollar book meets its highest funding cost of the year exactly when liquidity is thinnest — a risk not visible anywhere in the vol term structure.

tactical.score_interpretation: A net score of +0.4020 on a -1.00 to +1.00 scale is a firmly bullish tactical reading for the pair. Six factors are Bullish, two Bearish and two Neutral, with gross positive contributions of +0.4784 against gross negatives of -0.0764 — the negative block is only 16% of the positive block. Factor 1 alone supplies +0.1960, or 41% of the gross positive, and the top three contributors (Policy, Inflation & Growth, USD Funding) account for +0.3438 or 72%. tactical.rationale: At the applied tactical weights the analysis is dominated by three factors carrying 0.54 of the total — Policy & Rates at 0.28, Inflation & Growth at 0.15 and USD Liquidity at 0.11 — and all three point the same way for the pair. The reason they align is not narrative but arithmetic: the SNB policy rate is 0.00% and cannot change inside the window because the Governing Board does not meet until 24 September, while the Fed holds a 3.625% midpoint with three sitting hike dissenters, a 12 August CPI print that mechanically re-accelerates on the July energy reversal, and a funding market in which SOFR is printing exactly at IORB with the RRP buffer drained. The weighted result of +0.4020 with a 16%-to-84% negative-to-positive contribution ratio is the strongest directional reading available in the G10 dollar complex at this valuation date. The two standalone dossiers reinforce rather than conflict — the USD dossier is modestly bullish the dollar at conviction 2 and the CHF dossier is firmly bearish the franc at conviction 4 — and, critically, the USD dossier independently nominates USD/CHF as its own cleanest long-dollar expression on exactly this logic. The bilateral factors that modify those standalone views are three. First, the guidance divergence is larger bilaterally than either dossier's own weight implies, because a Fed actively rebuilding hawkish credibility against a central bank that has published a three-year forecast conditioned on doing nothing is the maximum available asymmetry in the developed world. Second, the commodity netting is unusually clean for this pair — oil up is +USD and -CHF, gold down is -CHF, with no third channel — so the terms-of-trade transfer works entirely in the pair's favour at current levels. Third, and cutting the other way, the US fiscal term premium is more dangerous here than in any other dollar cross, because the franc is the specific destination for reallocation out of a questioned reserve asset, and that mechanism has already produced one 1.05% single-session decline inside the last week. What is priced versus what we expect is the edge: the one-month forward outright is 0.80393, meaning the market pays a long-pair holder 27 pips simply for the differential, while we expect spot at 0.8170 — a 131-pip gap that compounds the carry rather than offsetting it, and which exists because consensus has extrapolated disinflation from a June US CPI print that was a compositional artefact of the post-ceasefire oil collapse. The path of least resistance over four weeks is a retest of the 0.8107-0.8139 rejection band and then the 0.8207 cycle high, because the medium-term MA stack is intact and rising and because there is no scheduled Swiss event capable of interrupting it. The dated catalysts that decide it are unusually dense and unusually one-sided in origin: US payrolls on 7 August, the EIA STEO on 11 August, US CPI on 12 August, the Hormuz transit-fee expiry around 16 August, the July FOMC minutes around 19 August, core PCE on 26 August and Jackson Hole on 27-29 August — seven US-driven events against one Swiss CPI print. The conviction driver is that the differential is observable today, is the widest in the G10, and is being earned at a 6.52% implied volatility with realised running above it. The conviction limiters are equally concrete: a crowded dollar long that has already been marked against, a failed breakout at the cycle high, and a fiscal term premium that has demonstrated it can break the yields-up-dollar-up link in this pair specifically.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net score of +0.1336 is a modestly bullish strategic reading and is exactly one-third of the tactical +0.4020. Five factors carry zero (Inflation & Growth, Risk Appetite, Event Risk, Market Structure and USD Funding, together 0.31 of the weight), so the score is generated by three positives — Policy at +0.1792, Guidance at +0.0792 and Flows at +0.0208, totalling +0.2792 — against two substantial negatives, External Balance at -0.0880 and Fiscal at -0.0576, totalling -0.1456. The negatives offset 52% of the gross positive, versus only 16% tactically. Conviction mapping places +0.1336 in the 0.10-0.20 band, giving conviction 2.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the framework redistributes materially and the redistribution is unfavourable. Policy & Rates holds at 0.28 and External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16 while Guidance rises from 0.07 to 0.12 and Fiscal from 0.06 to 0.09 — so the two factors on which Switzerland is structurally strongest gain 0.13 of weight while the factors on which the dollar is cyclically strongest either lose weight or turn Neutral. That is why the same underlying facts produce a score one-third the size. The dominant contributor remains Policy at +0.1792, and it is durable: the SNB's own conditional forecast conditions on 0.00% through 2028, the Fed's SEP median implies one more hike, and the projected differential reaches roughly 387.5bp by December. Guidance reinforces it, because the pair is long a central bank rebuilding hawkish credibility against one that has pre-committed to passivity, and 14 of 15 economists responding to an additional question said the SNB should increase currency interventions rather than cut rates — an SNB that intervenes only against franc strength sets a floor under the pair and supplies no upside. The conflicting inputs are External Balance and Fiscal, contributing -0.1456 between them, and they are causally linked rather than independent: a United States running a 2.9%-of-GDP external deficit and a 5.8%-of-GDP fiscal deficit at full employment, with a $38.6bn bilateral goods deficit specifically against Switzerland, faces a counterparty running a 9.77% surplus, a CHF 974bn net creditor position and a constitutional debt brake. That combination is the single reason a 362.5bp carry advantage has produced only 0.77% of appreciation over twelve months, and there is no reason to expect it to stop operating. What is priced versus what we expect is the clearest quantified edge in this analysis: the six-month forward outright is 0.78994 while we expect 0.8150, a 251-pip gap worth +3.11% on a forward expression, of which 167 pips is carry already embedded in the curve and 84 pips is our spot view. Consensus sits against us on the spot leg — UBS projects USD/CHF stabilising around 0.78 — but the market's own forward curve is the more conservative and more tradeable benchmark, and we differ from it by 251 pips. The path of least resistance is a slow grind within the established 0.76-0.825 range rather than a breakout, with the strongest phase between the September SEP and the 30 September appropriations cliff and the weakest through the November political cluster. The dated catalysts that decide it are the 16 September and 9 December FOMC meetings (both with SEPs), the 24 September and 10 December SNB assessments, the 29 September pharma tariff extension and appropriations expiry, and the 3 November midterms. Conviction is 2 rather than 3 because half the factor set supplies nothing, because the largest single negative carries the highest confidence in the set, and because on spot alone the six-month risk/reward is 0.27:1 — this is a carry harvest with a bounded expected spot gain and an unbounded tail loss, and it must be sized as such.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically USD/CHF slips from 1st to 2nd among long-dollar expressions, behind short EUR/USD. The reason is bilateral rather than dollar-specific: EUR/USD's counterparty runs a 1.15%-of-GDP current-account surplus against Switzerland's 9.77%, and carries a +209,326-contract asset-manager long that is the most extreme single position in the G10 and the most likely to capitulate on a hawkish US surprise, whereas the franc's structural surplus grows more binding as the horizon extends. It remains ahead of USD/JPY (a narrowing 195bp ten-year spread and a -2.53 risk reversal), USD/CAD (a 137.5bp differential with a fully priced BoC hold), and well ahead of USD/NOK, where the US ten-year premium has collapsed to 33bp and Norway runs a 15.59% surplus with an explicit Norges Bank hiking signal. Within the pair's own family, long USD/CHF versus short EUR/CHF is the cleanest strategic construction.

strategic.path_expectation: The strategic path is a stepped grind punctuated by the central-bank calendar, not a trend channel. Phase one, August into mid-September, should be the strongest: it contains the US CPI energy re-acceleration, the Hormuz transit expiry, and a 16 September FOMC carrying a Summary of Economic Projections that we expect to validate the hawkish framing — this is where the pair should clear 0.8107-0.8139 and retest the 0.8207 cycle high. Phase two, from the 24 September SNB assessment through mid-November, should be the weakest and is where we expect a 2-3% retracement: the SNB revises its conditional inflation forecast for the first time since the energy shock re-intensified, the pharma tariff extends to all importers on 29 September, and the US political cluster forms a dense pair-negative sequence with no offsetting positive catalyst. Pullbacks in that phase should find support at the 100-day, currently 0.79832 and rising, and we would build rather than reduce into them. Phase three, December into January, is the resolution: the 9 December FOMC carries the year's final SEP and the 10 December SNB assessment carries the full Monetary Policy Report, and they land immediately before the December year-end cross-currency basis turn, which is the most likely source of a sharp, short-lived 1-2% counter-trend franc rally that we would fade rather than follow. We expect realised volatility to rise from 6.9% toward the 7.18% implied by one-year options, so pullbacks should be deeper and more frequent than in the tactical window. Pattern shape: a rising staircase with a pronounced trough in the late-September-to-mid-November political window.

consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Three specific analytical points. First, the consensus bear case rests on Fed cuts, and we think that distribution is much thinner than it appears — a Committee that deleted its easing bias, carries three sitting hike dissenters and whose Chair has said he has no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation does not cut inside six months, which removes the primary mechanism by which the 362.5bp differential compresses. Second, consensus has not absorbed the structural reassignment of the franc from haven to funding currency, which was dated to the late-July SNB source reporting and is a persistent flow rather than a sentiment; funding-currency status keeps the quote leg heavy independent of Swiss fundamentals. Third, consensus applies the pre-shale correlation in which higher oil is dollar-negative, when in this specific bilateral the United States is a net energy exporter and Switzerland is a pure importer with zero domestic production, so Brent at $91.82 is a straightforward terms-of-trade transfer toward the base currency. Where we agree with the bears is on the structural argument: the 12.67-percentage-point current-account differential and the -$38.6bn bilateral goods deficit are real, they are why twelve months of 362.5bp carry produced 0.77% of appreciation, and they are why our strategic conviction is 2 rather than 4.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: A six-month long-pair forward returns approximately +3.11%, comprising +1.04% of spot and +2.07% of carry, measured against the 0.78994 outright.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If UBS is right and the pair converges toward 0.78, the spot loss of roughly 266 pips is offset to approximately -99 pips or -1.23% by carry — a tolerable outcome, and the reason this view is expressed in forwards rather than spot. The genuine risk is not consensus being right but the tail being realised: a 3-4% franc rally in a fortnight, the historical template for a funding-currency unwind, erases more than a year of carry.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The two horizons are aligned in stance and sharply divergent in intensity, with confidence falling from 60% to 58%. The stances agree because the driver — a 362.5bp differential against a pre-committed SNB — operates at both horizons. The magnitudes diverge because the weight schedule moves 0.13 of weight into External Balance and Fiscal, the two factors on which Switzerland is structurally strongest, while three of the tactically bullish factors (Inflation & Growth, Risk Appetite, USD Funding) turn Neutral as their transmission mechanisms exhaust. In plain terms: the carry works now and the balance sheet wins later.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The 16 September FOMC paired with the 24 September SNB assessment, an eight-day window containing the only two events capable of changing either leg of the differential inside the horizon — the FOMC either delivers the hike its own June median implies, and the SNB revises its conditional inflation forecast for the first time since the energy shock re-intensified.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Because the horizons agree in direction, the position does not need to be flipped mid-horizon, which materially improves after-cost economics. Concentrate the position in the tactical window where the expected return per unit of risk is highest, hold it through the 16-24 September central-bank pairing, and reduce size materially into the late-September-to-mid-November political trough unless the conviction ladder's increase conditions have been met. Forwards should mature before the December year-end basis turn.

catalysts.rationale: The bilateral netting is what makes this ambiguous rather than directional. This is the clearest example in the analysis of a factor whose bilateral sign depends on magnitude rather than direction.

catalysts.rationale: Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole, and a venue in which the base leg can reinforce guidance while the quote leg has no scheduled opportunity to respond before 24 September. catalysts.rationale: The pivotal scheduled event of the horizon for this pair. The June SEP median for end-2026 is 3.8%, implying one hike, and three members already voted for it on 29 July; September is the first meeting with an updated dot plot and is where the Committee must deliver or visibly abandon its own median. Delivery takes the differential from 362.5bp to 387.5bp against a quote-currency central bank that has published a three-year zero assumption — the maximum available policy divergence in the developed world.

catalysts.event: SNB Monetary Policy Assessment and news conference
catalysts.rationale: The only event capable of moving the quote leg materially, and the identified inflection point for the strategic thesis. The SNB revises its conditional inflation forecast — currently 0.6/0.6/0.7, conditioned on a 0.00% policy rate — for the first time since the energy shock re-intensified. An upward revision above 0.9% for 2027 validates the market's residual hawkish premium and is pair-negative; a downward revision toward 0.4% revives negative-rate speculation and is pair-positive. Also watch for any change to the one-directional intervention language, which currently sets a floor beneath the pair.

catalysts.event: Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs extend to all non-Annex-III importers; US FY2026 appropriations expire
catalysts.rationale: A rare date on which both legs take a hit simultaneously and in opposite directions for the pair. The tariff extension makes the Swiss drag economy-wide rather than concentrated in the seventeen largest firms, striking Switzerland's largest export line to its largest bilateral customer — pair-positive. The same date carries the US appropriations cliff, against a 2026 base rate that already includes a partial DHS shutdown from 14 February to 30 April, and US governance stress transmits to USD/CHF harder than to any other dollar cross because the franc is the primary alternative store of value — pair-negative.

All 435 House seats and a third of the Senate determine the fiscal and trade settings for the remainder of the presidential term, at a moment when judicial rulings have already voided the IEEPA tariff architecture and left roughly $166bn of refunds in dispute. Congressional control therefore has unusually direct implications for the revenue path underpinning the term premium currently sitting in the 30Y at 5.27%. For this specific pair the transmission runs through the long end rather than the front end, the channel that has already produced one 1.05% single-session decline.

catalysts.event: December FOMC with final SEP, followed on 2026-12-10 by SNB assessment with December Monetary Policy Report
catalysts.rationale: The two central banks report within twenty-four hours of each other, and it is the only such clustering in the horizon. The Fed must either deliver the 3.8% end-2026 median or mark it down; the SNB publishes its most information-rich release of the year, at which the market's residual +12bp of December hawkish franc premium is either paid or unwound. Both land immediately before the December year-end cross-currency basis turn, the single date on which a franc-funded long-dollar book is most vulnerable and which is unpriced in a smoothly rising vol curve.

invalidators.condition: US 30-year Treasury yield sustains above 5.50% for five consecutive sessions while ten-year breakevens remain below 2.35%, and USD/CHF simultaneously fails to make a new high
invalidators.mechanism: This combination isolates fiscal term premium from inflation compensation and confirms that the market is charging a rising risk premium on the reserve asset — and this specific pair is the G10's most fiscally exposed dollar cross, since the franc is the primary reserve-quality alternative when US sovereign quality is questioned. It already produced a 1.05% single-session pair decline on 30 July.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: US Treasury daily par yield curve 30-year alongside the FRED T10YIE series, plus USD/CHF's failure to confirm

invalidators.condition: Brent crude sustains above $115 per barrel for two consecutive weeks
invalidators.mechanism: That is the level at which the bilateral netting flips sign for this pair: below it the terms-of-trade transfer toward a net-energy-exporting United States and away from a pure-importing Switzerland dominates and the pair rises, while above it the franc's capital-flight haven beta overwhelms the energy channel — the threshold demonstrated by the March 2026 episode when Brent reached $126.69.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: EIA Europe Brent spot price series alongside VIX
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily for spot, weekly for the EIA series

invalidators.condition: USD/CHF closes below its 200-day moving average at 0.79042 on a weekly basis
invalidators.new_stance: Neutral tactically; strategic conviction reduced to 1
invalidators.mechanism: The 200-day is the pair's primary systematic regime line and a weekly close beneath it flips trend-following capital from long to short at the exact moment the crowded dollar leg has no fresh buyer beneath it, converting a supported grind into an unsupported one.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: USD/CHF spot versus the 200-day SMA, currently 2.05% above

invalidators.condition: The 24 September SNB assessment revises the 2027 conditional inflation forecast above 0.9% while the 16 September FOMC holds without a hike
invalidators.mechanism: That pairing validates the market's residual 12-25bp of hawkish franc premium and simultaneously invalidates the Fed's own 3.8% end-2026 median — the only sequence in which both legs of the 362.5bp differential move against the pair in the same eight-day window, breaking Factors 1 and 6 (0.35 tactical / 0.40 strategic weight) simultaneously.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SNB conditional inflation forecast for 2027 and the FOMC September SEP median for end-2026

invalidators.condition: The CFTC leveraged-fund net CHF position turns net long above +5,000 contracts for two consecutive weekly reports while the composite leveraged short in foreign currency simultaneously exceeds -280,000
invalidators.mechanism: This specific combination means the franc leg has flipped from funding currency back to haven while the dollar leg has become maximally crowded — the configuration in which the pair's positioning is one-sided on both legs and mean reversion historically dominates.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CFTC Traders in Financial Futures, Swiss franc net leveraged, alongside the seven-contract G10 composite
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Weekly, Friday for the prior Tuesday

invalidators.condition: Swiss headline CPI prints at or above 1.0% year-on-year with SFSO core inflation 1 simultaneously above 0.6% in any of the July, August or September releases while US core CPI stays at or below 2.6%
invalidators.mechanism: A broadening of the Swiss energy impulse into core would restore the franc's policy optionality and validate rather than unwind the front-end hawkish premium, compressing the real-rate differential from +62.5bp toward zero.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SFSO headline and core inflation 1 against BLS core CPI

signposts.indicator: USD/CHF spot relative to the 50-day and 200-day moving averages
signposts.confirms_if: Spot reclaims and holds above the 50-day at 0.80943 and subsequently clears the 0.8107-0.8139 rejection band
signposts.invalidates_if: A weekly close below the 200-day at 0.79042
signposts.bilateral_importance: This matters more for this pair than for either currency's TWI because USD/CHF is where the world's largest funding trade is expressed, so systematic flow around the moving-average stack is amplified by the size of the carry book sitting behind it.

signposts.indicator: Fed–SNB policy differential and the residual SNB hawkish premium
signposts.current_level: +362.5bp policy differential; roughly +12bp of SNB tightening priced by December and +24bp by March 2027 against a published 0.00% assumption
signposts.confirms_if: The differential widens toward 387.5bp on a September or December Fed hike while the SNB premium decays below +6bp
signposts.invalidates_if: The differential compresses below 325bp, either through Fed cut pricing or through validated SNB tightening
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the pair's entire transmission mechanism — USD/CHF is more nearly a pure expression of the Fed-SNB spread than any other G10 cross, because there is no intervening commodity, equity or trade channel of comparable strength.
signposts.frequency: At each FOMC (eight per year) and each SNB assessment (four per year)

signposts.indicator: US 30-year Treasury yield versus ten-year breakeven inflation
signposts.confirms_if: The 30Y falls back below 5.10%, or breakevens rise above 2.45% so the long-end move becomes an inflation story rather than a fiscal one
signposts.invalidates_if: The 30Y sustains above 5.50% with breakevens below 2.35%
signposts.bilateral_importance: This matters more for USD/CHF than for any other dollar cross because Switzerland is the G10's only counterparty with a AAA rating, a 37.6% debt ratio and a constitutional debt brake — it is the specific destination for capital reallocating out of a questioned reserve asset.

signposts.current_level: $91.82/bbl (27 July), up 30.3% from $70.46 at end-June and 25.0% above its year-ago level
signposts.confirms_if: Brent holds an $85-110 range — high enough to sustain the US net-exporter terms-of-trade gain and the Swiss import cost, low enough that the risk channel stays dormant
signposts.invalidates_if: Sustained above $115 (the franc's capital-flight channel dominates) OR below $75 (the terms-of-trade transfer disappears entirely)
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the only signpost in the set whose sign flips at a threshold rather than a direction, because the two currencies sit on opposite sides of the energy trade while sharing a haven function.
signposts.frequency: Weekly for the EIA series, daily marks in Today in Energy

signposts.current_level: $4,054.45, down 12.14% over three months and 17.94% over six from a February peak of $5,277.88
signposts.confirms_if: Gold stays below $4,400, keeping the debasement-and-uncertainty haven complex in drawdown alongside the franc
signposts.invalidates_if: A sustained break above $4,600, signalling structural re-engagement of the haven bid that historically pulls the franc with it
signposts.bilateral_importance: Gold is the franc's correlated haven asset and the dollar's competing store of value simultaneously, making it the cleanest cross-asset read on which side of this pair the market is choosing.

signposts.indicator: SNB sight deposits of domestic banks
signposts.current_level: CHF 442.66bn (week to 24 July), up CHF 9.6bn (+2.2%) over three months; total sight deposits CHF 469.27bn
signposts.confirms_if: Flat to modestly rising, within +CHF 5bn over any four-week window

signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the only observable measure of official-sector flow in either leg of the pair, and it is asymmetric — the SNB acts against franc strength but never against franc weakness, so a change here is the earliest evidence the pair's floor is being removed.

signposts.current_level: Reserves $2,944,541mn (29 July), -$355.2bn year-on-year; SOFR 3.65% exactly at IORB of 3.65%, 75th percentile 3.70%; ON RRP drained to ~$2bn

signposts.invalidates_if: Reserves rebuild above $3.05tn as Desk bill purchases and TGA normalisation restore abundance
signposts.bilateral_importance: USD/CHF is now the principal funding pair in the G10 — dollar asset leg, franc liability leg — so the relative cost of the two legs transmits here more directly than to any other cross.
signposts.frequency: Weekly, Thursday, as of the prior Wednesday

assumptions: All price-derived figures — spot 0.8066, 1M/3M/6M/1Y performance, the 52-week range and percentile, the 50/100/200-day SMAs, trend regime and recent price action — come exclusively from the provided Twelve Data daily OHLC series (390 observations, 2025-06-02 to 2026-08-06); the valuation date is 2026-08-01 while the price series extends to 2026-08-06, and we use the 6 August close of 0.8066 as spot throughout, noting the two dossiers' internal spot reference of 0.80779 (31 July close) differs by 12 pips.

Support, resistance and chart patterns are drawn from web technical sources because visual chart levels cannot be derived from raw OHLC; where sources disagree they are presented as ranges rather than reconciled, and the 0.8107-0.8139 resistance band and the 0.8065-0.8076 hourly moving-average support cluster are both single-sourced.

Bilateral trade figures are taken directly from the injected IMF DOTS block; the reporting asymmetry between US-reported imports of $63.7bn and Swiss-reported exports of $73.5bn (a ~$9.8bn gap) is disclosed and attributed to pharmaceutical and non-monetary gold flows through Switzerland's refining hub; we use the US-reported net figure of -$38.6bn.

All implied volatilities and risk reversals originate from the CHF dossier's single-dealer snapshot (Saxo Bank OTC FX Options Analytics, 31 July 2026, 07:00 GMT), which itself flags intraday drift on a re-fetch; no second-dealer corroboration was available, and the one-year IV percentile of ~45 is an estimate inferred from the realised-volatility distribution rather than a measured percentile.

The three-month USD/CHF cross-currency basis — the single most direct measure of the funding channel Factor 10 assesses — is not obtainable from BIS, ECB, SNB, the Federal Reserve, FRED or any free venue; Factor 10 substitutes the SOFR-IORB spread, swap-line usage and standing repo facility usage, and Factor 10 confidence is capped at 58/50 accordingly.

The two dossiers use different US ten-year yields (CHF dossier 4.67% FRED 29 July vs USD dossier 4.75% Treasury par curve 31 July); we use the Treasury figure throughout as fresher and primary, producing a +427.5bp ten-year differential against the CHF dossier's +419.5bp; the Swiss 2Y of 0.14% is single-sourced and the +414bp front-end differential is indicative.

Forward points are mid-market from published bid/ask and were re-based from the dossier's 0.80779 spot reference to our 0.8066 spot; the disclosed wedge of forward-implied annualised franc appreciation (3.97-4.12%) exceeding the 362.5bp policy spread by 34-49bp is attributable to SARON fixing below zero, US money-market rates above the funds midpoint, and the unobservable basis; the CHF dossier notes a later fetch of the same live page returned different points, so forward figures carry a same-session flag.
Weight adjustments are documented with per-factor reasons; six factors were adjusted, all within the ±0.05 limit, and both tactical and strategic columns sum to exactly 1.00.

Scoring convention: Bullish = +1, Neutral = 0, Bearish = -1, expressed in PAIR direction (rising USD/CHF); confidence-adjusted score = stance × confidence/100; weighted contribution = confidence-adjusted score × weight; conviction maps from |net score| per stated bands; both weighted-score tables reconcile exactly to their stated net scores.

Scenario probabilities (50/25/25 at both horizons) are analyst judgements rather than option-implied, because no full volatility smile was obtainable for this pair; expected spot levels of 0.8170 and 0.8150 are likewise judgements measured against market forward points applied to the provided spot.

Inherited dossier limitations propagate here: from the USD dossier, the BIS five-year REER average discrepancy and unverified sovereign ratings; from the CHF dossier, the VIX level discrepancy (17.09 cached vs 17.64 secondary check), the Brent level discrepancy, the stale Morningstar DBRS AAA confirmation (379 days), the 2024-vintage 37.6% debt ratio, the 57-day-stale SNB OIS snapshot underpinning the 12-25bp hawkish-premium claim, and a withdrawn USD/CHF 50-day SMA figure; confidence has been set to reflect this uncertainty rather than the point estimate.

No dated, multi-bank USD/CHF consensus grid at 3M/6M/12M horizons could be sourced; the consensus section therefore benchmarks primarily against the market's own forward curve, which is fully verifiable, and secondarily against individually obtainable published views — a narrower consensus base than would be available for EUR/USD or USD/JPY.
